punchline: A journalist who wrote about comfort walked thirty-three days through the Alaskan Arctic and came back arguing for small chosen hardships, not suffering.
thirty_sec: Michael Easter argued that modern life had engineered discomfort out of our days. To test it, he joined a caribou hunt on foot in the Alaskan Arctic: thirty-three days, a heavy pack, no phone signal, food depending on the hunt. He did not decide that pain is good. He found that chosen, purposeful difficulty woke capacities he usually leaves idle. The Comfort Crisis tells the story.
